title: Dative 2: Giving and Sending (Verbs of Transfer)
description: Verbs of giving and transferring (давать, дарить, покупать, писать, посылать) take a dative recipient. Drill the recipient form across genders.
descriptionRussian: Глаголы передачи (давать, дарить, покупать, писать, посылать) ставят получателя в дательный падеж. Сегодня — отработка форм получателя.
intro: These verbs take two objects at once, which is the first time you have had to build a sentence with both. The thing being handed over goes in the accusative you already know; the person receiving it goes in the dative you learned last lesson. Both endings at the same time, in one sentence. That is the only new thing today.
rules: Verbs of giving and transferring (давать/дать, дарить, покупать, писать, посылать) take a dative recipient: давать книгу брату, писать письмо другу.
The structure is: subject + verb + accusative thing + dative recipient. Word order is flexible, but the dative recipient is always in the dative form regardless of position.
Form rules from Lesson 1 still apply: masc consonant + -у, fem -а / -я → -е, neuter -о → -у, neuter -е → -ю.
examples: Маша даёт книгу брату. (Masha gives a book to brother.) брат → брату.
Антон дарит цветы сестре. (Anton gives flowers to sister.) сестра → сестре.
Я пишу письмо другу. (I write a letter to friend.) друг → другу.
Лена покупает подарок Маше. (Lena buys a gift for Masha.) Маша → Маше.
Антон посылает посылку сыну. (Anton sends a parcel to son.) сын → сыну.

tables.title: Giving Verbs and the Dative Recipient

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: feminine -а changes to which letter in the dative?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1: помогать takes a dative complement. Feminine -а swaps to -е → маме. Today's lesson uses the same form rule for a new family of verbs: giving and sending.

items.promptEnglish: I give the book to brother.
items.hint: Брат is masculine consonant. The dative ending is...?
items.explanation: Давать takes the structure: давать что (acc) кому (dat). The book is the direct object (книгу = acc), and the recipient is dative: брат → брату. The recipient is who the book is going TO.

items.hint: Сестра is feminine -а. What replaces -а in the dative?
items.explanation: Дарить (to give as a gift) follows the same dat-recipient pattern. Сестра is feminine -а: -а → -е → сестре. Russians use дарить for occasions: birthdays, holidays, expressions of affection.

items.promptEnglish: I'm writing a letter to my friend.
items.hint: Recall the masculine pattern from Q1.2.
items.explanation: Писать takes a dative recipient when you're writing TO someone: писать кому. Друг → другу. Notice that 'писать о ком/чём' (write ABOUT something) uses the prepositional, not the dative.

items.promptEnglish: Lena is buying a gift for Masha.
items.hint: Маша is feminine -а. The beneficiary of a buy goes in the dative.
items.explanation: Покупать кому что means 'to buy something for someone'; the beneficiary is dative. Маша → Маше. The 'для + gen' alternative ('подарок для Маши') also works, but the dative is more conversational.

items.promptEnglish: I'm giving the book to Anton.
items.hint: Антон is a masculine consonant name. Apply the masculine rule.
items.explanation: Names follow the same rule as common nouns. Антон is masculine consonant, so it adds -у: Антону.

blanks: Антон посылает письмо _____. (Anton is sending a letter to his son.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Сын is masculine consonant. The recipient of посылать (to send) goes in the dative: + -у → сыну.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I am writing a long letter to my son.
errorCorrection.explanation: With писать, the thing written is the accusative (письмо) and the addressee is the dative: писать что кому. Сын is masculine consonant, so the dative is сыну. The bare nominative сын can only be a subject.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон дарит цветы бабушку на день рождения.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton gives flowers to his grandmother for her birthday.
errorCorrection.explanation: Дарить takes an accusative gift and a dative recipient: дарить что кому. The gift цветы is the accusative; the recipient бабушка goes in the dative, бабушке. Бабушку is the accusative, a slip that treats the grandmother as the gift.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is buying a beautiful gift for Sonya.
errorCorrection.explanation: Покупать кому что puts the beneficiary in the dative: Соня → Соне. Сони is the genitive, which would be correct only with the preposition для ('подарок для Сони'); without для, the bare dative Соне is the right form.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I give the book to brother.
minimalPairs.explanation: The recipient of давать goes in the dative: брату. The nominative брат would be a subject: 'Брат читает' (Brother is reading).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I'm writing a letter to friend.
minimalPairs.explanation: Писать кому puts the addressee in the dative: другу. Compare with писать о ком ('write about someone') which uses the prepositional: о друге.

reviewVocab.definition: to give as a gift (the recipient goes in the dative: дарить кому что)
to send (the recipient goes in the dative: посылать кому что)
recipient (the person receiving the gift, letter, or call; always in the dative)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша даёт книгу брату' получатель — это брат.
